Preprint (arXiv)
University of Notre Dame (8 authors); IBM Research (Chen, Gao); Tencent AI Lab (Liang)

Proposes an approach (TellOnce: drop-in layer turning user corrections into persistent, scoped, revisable behavioural rules with compiled runtime checks); secondary: compares (against No Memory, Mem0, PGMem, Zoro on three benchmarks, plus an access-compliance diagnostic of five rule-provision conditions)

TellOnce (version Not stated; experimental execution layer for Codex and Claude Code; released plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI). Baselines: No Memory, Mem0, PGMem, Zoro (versions Not stated). Diagnostic conditions: No Rules, All Rules, Mem0, Relevant Rules, Compiled Rules

Rule library: each rule holds the user requirement, scope (global/project), conditions, exceptions and supporting feedback quotes; per-rule compiled check specification (applicability, stage pre_action/artifact/delivery, required evidence, compliance/violation criteria) as programmatic or LLM-based check, or guidance-only, or inactive; 3-9 validation cases per check

Detect correction signal -> interpret with same-session context -> decide persistence and scope -> reconcile with library (reuse/revise/replace/add) -> compile check and validate (independent LLM labelling, up to 3 rounds) -> at each user turn select applicable rules and inject as guidance -> check at pre-action, artifact and delivery stages -> block or request revision (up to 3 repairs per input; one appeal)
User corrections are the input (simulated users in the experiments); no human review of learned rules or checks; validation of checks by a separate LLM call
Single artefact type (learned rule library and its checks, comparable to persistent agent rules/context files) inside a full agent run; rule-library use ablated at test time
Not classifiable (authors' wording: 'behavioral rules', 'personalization layer'; rules learned from feedback, not a specification written before code)

ClawArena scenarios (workspace tasks with multiple-choice and execution checks), MemoryArena group travel planning, SWE-Together repository-level coding problems with multi-turn interaction (existing code bases); diagnostic: 19 coding tasks from real transcripts

ClawArena: 8 learning / 16 test scenarios (240 / 474 questions). MemoryArena: 30 learning / 60 test tasks (211 / 415 questions). SWE-Together: 60 learning / 49 test tasks from 26 repository/task groups. Diagnostic: 19 tasks, 29 preference checks from 32 transcripts (~1M tokens each), 142 correction-conflict records
General agent workspace tasks, travel planning, software repositories (e.g. Hyperswitch); preferences on cleanup, workflow constraints, stylistic conventions

Simulated users (three fixed preference profiles; general task-improvement simulator for SWE-Together); simulator validated against five real AI researchers (790 judgments); diagnostic from a single user's transcripts
None measured (authors note added computation not matched across methods); resource limits listed (Table 9)

Native task score: ClawArena pooled binary correctness per round; MemoryArena native travel-plan correctness; SWE-Together first- and final-delivery task quality score with executable repository evidence
None
None measured (aim is fewer repeated corrections, measured indirectly via violation rate)

Preference violation rate (% of evaluation units with >= 1 confirmed violation of an applicable preference); diagnostic compliance rate; component diagnostics (admission recall 94.2%, structural accuracy 175/192, rule-update accuracy 15/16, check validation agreement 98.3%); simulator fidelity F1 0.906

Automatic: native benchmark scorers and execution checks; preference violations scored by an LLM evaluator (GPT-6 Luna, low reasoning) blind to method identity and memory; diagnostic checks manually annotated by one author and audited by a second

Values: task score / violation % (mean +- SD over 3 simulated users). Auxiliary calls GPT-6 Luna. Draft verdict rule: quality works if violation < 30 and task score not below best baseline by > 2; cost not measured for any configuration.

Benchmarks: ClawArena, MemoryArena group_travel_planner, SWE-Together with fixed hash-based whole-task learning/test splits. 5 methods x 3 solvers x 3 user profiles x 2 benchmarks (90 test groups). Baseline: No Memory (plus Mem0, PGMem, Zoro). Held constant: learning tasks and order, feedback policy (max one correction per question), harness, tools, auxiliary model GPT-6 Luna; feedback text differs per method (responds to actual behaviour). State frozen at test; no corrections at test (SWE-Together keeps within-task interaction up to 16 deliveries). Acceptance: native benchmark scorers + blind LLM preference evaluator. Repetitions: 3 simulated users (main); 3 runs (SWE-Together). Human intervention: none (simulated users). Computation not matched across methods

TellOnce lowest violation in all six settings: vs PGMem (best baseline) -19.3 to -42.3 points on ClawArena (e.g. 73.6 -> 34.7 Luna; 81.5 -> 39.2 Sol) and -3.0 to -22.9 on MemoryArena (12.6-14.5%). Task scores within ~1.6 points of the strongest baseline (not higher). Ablations: selection -1.0 to -4.8 points; checking/intervention -15 to -16 points on ClawArena, -0.7 to -2.7 on MemoryArena; final repair -2.1 to -5.2 (Claw). SWE-Together first delivery +1.8 (Luna) / +1.6 (Sol); final +0.6 / +5.4. Diagnostic: compiled rules 70.1% vs 54-55% plain rules. No significance tests

Distinguished methods on violation rate clearly (large gaps vs SD), not on task score (differences within noise). Repeatability: SD over 3 users, sometimes large (e.g. All Rules as Text Luna Claw +-18.8). Limitations stated: simulated users; fixed models and tasks; rule-update evaluation only in controlled diagnostics; extra computation not matched

Simulated feedback cannot capture real long-term collaboration; fixed set of models and benchmarks; ambiguous corrections hard to interpret; not every requirement checkable, semantic checks may err; rule revision evaluated only in controlled diagnostics; added computation not matched; future: long-term adaptation in real deployments
